top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation is a new chemical principle, event-driven catalytic removal of a chosen protein by a designed molecule that recruits an E3 ligase, and it has been reproduced independently in many laboratories. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated it, and Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligand and ternary-complex work made it a design discipline. A citation limited to bifunctional degraders keeps names and words matched. The weaknesses are real: no PROTAC is approved, and Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Kim and Gray are excluded. P002 follows because it shares the science but moves the prize toward the cereblon glue strand, where credit is spread. P004 and P003 add a second part with a single-name credit (Shokat; Cullis) that understates the teams involved, and both drop Ciulli.
